Carbene Reactivity in Cyclopropanation and Doyle−Kirmse

Yifan Zhang,<sup>#</sup> Shuang Li,<sup>#</sup> Hongzhu Chen,<sup>#</sup> Wei Song,<sup>#</sup> Yongquan Ning,* Zeyun Liu, Yong Wu,
Karunanidhi Murali, Paramasivam Sivaguru, and Xiaolong Zhang*
ABSTRACT: Herein, we developed the new, powerful, and easy-to-handle chemical reagent, dimethoxyacetaldehyde-N-
triftosylhydrazone (DMHz-Tfs), as a convenient in situ source of dimethoxydiazoethane under mild conditions. We demonstrate

elucidated the involvement of the most stable doublet spin state iron-carbene intermediate over other possible spin states.

Under the optimized conditions, the generality of the
reaction was then examined (Scheme 4A). A wide range of aryl
allyl sulfides containing either electron-donating or electron-
withdrawing substituents at the para- or meta-positions of the
aromatic ring were compatible, afording corresponding
products 50−57 in 63 to 98% yields. The steric hindrance
on the aromatic ring impacted the product yields, as ortho-
substituted aryl allyl sulfides produced slightly lower yields
(58−60). The reaction was also amenable to disubstituted aryl
allyl sulfides to deliver the desired products in moderate to
good yields (61−63). Allyl sulfides bearing electron-rich
naphthalene and furan rings smoothly participated in the
process, delivering 64 and 65 in 59% and 58% yields,
respectively. Besides aryl allyl sulfides, methyl, benzyl, and
adamantyl allyl sulfides were also suitable for this conversion,
which could react with DMHz-Tfs to obtain corresponding
products 66−68 in moderate to good yields. Similarly, the
reaction using 2-methylallyl, 1-phenylallyl, and 1,1-dimethy
lallyl aryl sulfides was also attempted, furnishing the desired
products in moderate to good yield (69−71). It is worth
noting that diallyl sulfide can efectively engage in the reaction,
yielding the desired bilateral [2,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement
product 72 (98% yield and d.r. = 1.5:1) by doubling other
reagents.
We then expanded the scope of this reaction to propargyl
sulfides 48 (Scheme 4B), which ofered a convenient route to
functionalized allenes.<sup>21</sup>
Aryl propargyl sulfides bearing a
methyl or methoxy group at the para-position of the aryl ring
and naphthyl propargyl sulfide could be converted smoothly
into the corresponding allenyl sulfides 73−76 in moderate to
good yields (49−68%). The reaction could proceed efectively
with 1-methyl or 1-trimethylsilyl substituted alkynyl sulfides,
which delivered target products 77 and 78 in 96% and 91%
yield, respectively. Finally, we explored the versatility of the
acetal-substituted homoallyl sulfide product 49. The mild acid
hydrolysis of 49 produced the corresponding aldehyde analog
79 (92% yield), which then was oxidized in the presence of m-
CPBA to give sulfone derivative 80 in 90% yield (Scheme 4C).

In this work, we developed a new chemical reagent, DMHz-
Tfs, which could slowly release dimethoxydiazoethane in situ
under mild conditions. Its carbene reactivity was established in
iron-catalyzed cyclopropanation and Doyle−Kirmse reactions,
enabling access to various acetal functionalized cyclopropanes
and homoallyl- and allenyl-sulfides. The broad applicability of
the developed protocol was highlighted by the late-stage
modification of complex bioactive molecules, gram-scale
synthesis, and structural diversification of acetal functionalized
products. DFT studies disclosed that the doublet spin state of
the iron catalyst enabled the carbene transfer process. Given its
ease of preparation, high stability, and operational safety,
DMHz-Tfs are expected to have a high potential for carbene
transfer reactions.
